transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I guess what finally pushed me to make an appointment is... well, I feel a little silly even bringing it up, because I know everyone gets busy and stressed, but I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. I'm a software developer, and there are just so many things competing for my attention right now—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions. 

I try to stay on top of it, I really do, but I just end up starting whatever is loudest, you know? Like, whatever is right in my face, instead of focusing on what actually matters or what's most important. 

I hope I'm explaining that right. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job at work, and I feel bad that I can't seem to juggle it all like I'm supposed to. Does that... make sense? Is that the sort of thing you usually help people with?
Did you have these same kinds of trouble with attention or organization when you were a child?

Um, well... yes, I suppose I did. I mean, I was a good kid, I really tried to do what I was told, you know? But looking back... yeah, I guess this was there in grade school, too. 

My teachers were always very kind about it. They always wrote on my report cards that I was bright, which was really nice of them to say! But... they also usually noted that I daydreamed a lot. And I’d, um... I’d lose my homework folders pretty often. The embarrassing part is, I would actually finish the assignments—I really did do the work!—but I’d just... forget to take it out of my bag and turn it in. 

And all of that was happening long before I was even a teenager. I feel a little bad admitting all that, like I should have just tried harder to be organized back then. Is that... is that the kind of information you need? Am I answering your question okay?
Do these same organization and attention problems also cause trouble for you outside of work?

Um... outside of work? Well, I mean, I try really hard to keep my personal life running smoothly. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, you know? 

I guess... well, I haven't really noticed it being a huge issue at home. I mean, my wife is incredibly organized, she's just wonderful at keeping track of things, so maybe she just handles a lot of the details. I try to help out as much as I can, of course! I really do. But I don't think I have the same level of... chaos... at home as I do at work. 

Or at least, I hope I don't. I try to keep things tidy and stay on top of the bills and everything. I might forget to put a dish away here or there, but nothing major, I don't think. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong idea, I just... I don't want to make it sound like my whole life is a mess, because I really do try my best to keep it together.
When your wife is not handling the details at home, do you still have trouble keeping track of things?

Um... well, I guess... if I'm being completely honest, when she's not around to kind of keep an eye on things, I do misplace things a bit. I mean, everyone does, right? It's totally normal to lose your keys sometimes! 

But... I guess it does happen to me kind of a lot. I'm always—well, maybe not *always*, but very often—hunting around for things I need for work. Like my USB-C adapters, or my stylus, or my sketchbook... even my work badge. I'll just set them down without thinking, and then I have absolutely no memory of where they went. 

It's so silly, really. I know I just need to put things back in their proper place. But sometimes it takes me so long to find them that it kind of derails my whole morning. I try really hard not to let it happen, I promise I do, I just... I get so frustrated with myself. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not making myself sound completely incompetent.
Has forgetting or losing things at home ever caused a real problem for you?

Um... a real problem? Well, I wouldn't say a *real* problem. I mean, I try very hard to make sure my little slip-ups don't actually hurt anyone or cause any major disasters, you know? 

I guess... well, there might be a little friction sometimes. My wife is so patient, she really is an angel, but I know it can be a tiny bit annoying for her when I'm running around looking for my wallet right when we're supposed to be leaving for dinner. I always apologize profusely, of course! And I really do try to be better about it. 

But as for causing a real, serious problem? No, I don't think so. I always manage to find what I need eventually, or I find a workaround. I'd hate to think my absentmindedness was actually causing genuine trouble for my family. Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different areas of your life?

Um... worrying excessively? Well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I care about my work and my family, naturally—I want to do a good job and be a good husband. But I wouldn't say I'm always worrying about everything. 

I try really hard to just stay positive and take things as they come. I definitely don't want to be one of those people who brings everyone down with a lot of anxiety or stress, you know? So... no, I don't think I have that issue. I just try to do my best and keep a good attitude. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering exactly what you're looking for.
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stress at work or in your life?

Um... a specific stress? No, I don't think so. I mean, work is work, right? There are always deadlines and projects, but nothing out of the ordinary. And things at home are really wonderful. 

I don't think there was any big event or sudden change that made things worse. Honestly, I feel like I've always been a little bit like this... just kind of scattered sometimes. I've always tried my best to manage it, and I think I've done a pretty okay job, mostly. I definitely wouldn't blame any of this on outside stress or anything like that. I take full responsibility for my own little quirks! 

Does that sound right to you? I just want to make sure I'm not missing some connection you might be looking for.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in grade school and persisting into adulthood, including daydreaming, losing homework/materials, failing to turn in completed work, disorganization, prioritizing whatever is most immediately salient, and frequently misplacing important items. Symptoms occur across settings (school history, work, and home when spouse is not compensating) and cause clear occupational impairment, with some interpersonal friction at home. Anxiety and stress-related explanations were not supported, and there was no specific psychosocial trigger.
